business_scope.primary_industry_name: Industrial Quick-Freezing of Steamed Dim Sum and Dumplings

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (Unitary National Jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid Civil Law (codified Napoleonic model) with Islamic Sharia as the principal source of legislation under Article 2 of the Egyptian Constitution (2014, amended 2019)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt-United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 1986, in force 1992)
Egypt-United Kingdom Agreement on the Promotion and Protection of Investments
Egypt-United Arab Emirates Bilateral Investment Treaty
Egypt-European Union Association Agreement (in force 2004, investment protection provisions)
Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements with China, UK, Germany, France, Kuwait, and the UAE

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002, as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014 and Law No. 144 of 2019; Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 1899 of 2003 (as amended); Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2310 of 2017); Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976; Financial Regulatory Authority Board Resolutions on AML/CFT controls for UBO identification; Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT regulations applicable to banking payment rails.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of the valid passport or national ID of each natural-person shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country notary public with legalization by the home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization route (Egypt is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention): (1) notarization by the home-country notary; (2) legalization by the home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs; (3) final legalization by the Embassy of Egypt in the home country. Apostilles issued by foreign authorities are not accepted for Egyptian registry purposes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming account relationship and standing of each founding shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing commercial bank, with the signatory banker's capacity authenticated by the local chamber of commerce or notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization route: notarization, home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization, then legalization by the Egyptian Embassy or Consulate having consular jurisdiction over the issuing bank.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or certificate of registration for any corporate shareholder (if the shareholder is a legal person)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or equivalent commercial registrar in the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization route: issued by the foreign registry, authenticated by the home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and legalized by the Egyptian Embassy or Consulate. A backdated certificate older than 90 days at the date of the GAFI one-stop-shop filing must be re-issued.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the Egyptian incorporation agent for the GAFI one-stop-shop filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of residence of each grantor (shareholder or director)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization route: notarization, home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization, and Egyptian Embassy legalization. If executed inside Egypt, the POA must be authenticated before the Egyptian Notary Authority.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of every shareholder, director, secretary, and UBO against: (i) the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (ii) the US OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists; (iii) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list; and (iv) the Egyptian domestic terrorist entities designation list issued under Law No. 8 of 2015. Domestic and foreign PEPs trigger enhanced due diligence (EDD), including source-of-wealth documentation, senior management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring under the MLTFCU guidelines. Screening results, negative news, and EDD conclusions are archived in the AML compliance file; the frozen food processing activity with SWIFT LC/TT rails is classified as Low Risk Standard and does not exempt the filer from any screening obligation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI One-Stop-Shop company incorporation portal and automated name reservation module (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones), cross-linked to the Unified Commercial Registry database of the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade; accessible through the GAFI e-services portal at www.gafi.gov.eg.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory company name must be registered in Arabic under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981. A Latin-script transliteration is permitted only as a convenience name for banking, customs, and export documentation and does not constitute the statutory trade name. Foreign brand words (e.g., DIM SUM) must be rendered phonetically in Arabic script without creating a misleading trade description, and any trademark-derived element must be cleared against the Egyptian Trade Marks Register.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Finance, Insurance, Securities, Capital: prohibited unless the entity holds a prior license from the Central Bank of Egypt or the Financial Regulatory Authority
National, Central, Arab Republic, Misr (Egypt): require explicit ministerial or GAFI delegated authorization and are generally reserved for public-sector or strategic entities
Military, Police, Armed, Sovereign, Intelligence: absolutely prohibited
Islamic, Jihad, Christian, or any religious-denominational reference: prohibited on public order grounds
Political party names, state organ designations, foreign government emblems: prohibited
Words contrary to public morality or implying a regulated industrial activity for which the entity has no license
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation that expires cannot be automatically extended; the applicant re-submits a fresh reservation request with a new fee. Upon rejection, the GAFI legal unit issues a written reason (similarity, prohibition, or public order). The applicant may file a written grievance with the GAFI Legal Affairs Department within 15 working days of the rejection notice. If the grievance is denied or unanswered, an administrative appeal may be lodged before the Egyptian Council of State (Administrative Court) within 60 days, with interim relief available in urgent cases. Filing two alternative Arabic names in parallel is the recommended commercial practice to avoid delays in the LLC establishment schedule.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for ISIC 1074 frozen food manufacturing. The Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and the National Food Safety Authority (NFSA) licensing regime require a physical registered office and an operational production facility within Egypt, including cold-chain infrastructure for quick-freezing and frozen storage of dim sum and dumplings. A virtual mailbox or shared address without on-site premises will cause rejection at the NFSA pre-licensing stage and will be deemed a false declaration before the Commercial Registry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (approximately 90% within the first 12 months). GAFI verifies the registered office and the legalized lease at incorporation; the NFSA under Law No. 1 of 2017 conducts pre-license premise inspections and unannounced sanitation and cold-chain audits; the Industrial Control Authority may inspect production lines during factory registration and export licensing. The registered address must coincide with the actual headquarters or, at minimum, with a dedicated local administrative office staffed during business hours.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended (LLC provisions), Executive Regulations No. 542 of 1981, and Investment Law No. 72 of 2017
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Investor One-Stop Shop, in coordination with the Commercial Registry, Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Association and Incorporation Application for a Limited Liability Company (Request for Establishment of an LLC under Law 159/1981)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed for LLCs under the current Egyptian legal framework; the founders freely set the capital in the Articles. The capital must be fully subscribed, and the paid-up portion, as stated in the Articles, must be evidenced by a bank deposit certificate before the issuance of the Commercial Registry extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The incorporators adopt the company's Articles of Association as notarized. (2) The registered office is set at 121 Industrial Zone Road, Ain Sokhna, Suez Governorate, Egypt. (3) The initial subscribed capital of EGP 500,000 is taken by the founding shareholders and shall be deposited in a dedicated bank account. (4) [Name] is appointed as first manager and legal representative, authorized to complete Commercial Registry, tax and social insurance registrations. (5) The manager is empowered to process the industrial and environmental licensing of the prefabricated dim sum factory.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation and legal form pre-approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Center / GAFI online pre-registration portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three alternative corporate names in Arabic and/or English to GAFI, specifying the legal form as a Limited Liability Company and the intended industrial activities. Pay the name reservation fee and obtain the name reservation certificate, which is valid for 90 days. The certificate must be presented in all subsequent incorporation steps.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Copy of each founder's national ID or passport
Power of attorney if the application is signed by an agent
Declaration of the intended activity code ISIC 1074 / frozen dim sum production
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a proposed name is rejected for conflict, similarity, or illegality, file a written grievance with the GAFI complaint unit and submit a revised list of three alternative names; the objection is resolved within five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and notarization of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office (Office of Authenticity) under the Egyptian Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a licensed Egyptian counsel to draft the Arabic-language Articles of Association. The deed must include the corporate form (LLC), company name, registered office address, purpose (manufacturing of frozen prepared dim sum products), capital, classes of shares, partners' percentages, management and representation rules, and dispute resolution provisions. All founders or their lawful attorneys must appear before the Notary Public to authenticate the deed and receive the notarization official number.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association in Arabic
GAFI name reservation certificate
Valid national ID or passport of each founder
Authenticated power of attorney for any signatory
Proof of lawful seat: lease contract or title deed for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary Public objects to the content, authenticity, or conformity of the deed, counsel corrects and re-files the deed without a new corporate fee; a fresh notarial appointment is made at the next available session.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation filing, Commercial Registry extraction, and issuance of the incorporation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Investor One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Articles of Association to the GAFI one-stop shop together with all required dossiers and the state filing fee. GAFI verifies legal compliance, issues the incorporation decision, and automatically transmits the establishment data to the Commercial Registry. Upon completion, GAFI issues the incorporation certificate and the official Commercial Registry extract, and the company receives a provisional taxpayer identification number.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Association and the required number of authentic copies
GAFI name reservation certificate
Lease contract or title deed of the registered office
Bank certificate evidencing the paid-up portion of the capital
Partners' resolution appointing the first manager
Copies of national IDs or passports of founders and manager
Economic project and preliminary manufacturing summary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a defect notice or asks for additional documents, the applicant must cure the filing within 30 calendar days using the same case number. If the incorporation request is rejected, an administrative appeal may be filed before the GAFI Grievance Committee within 60 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration, corporate bank capital deposit, and social insurance registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Social Insurance Authority (SIA), and a licensed commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the name of the LLC and deposit the paid-up capital. Submit the Commercial Registry extract and incorporation certificate to the Egyptian Tax Authority to obtain a permanent tax card and VAT registration for the production and sale of frozen foods. Register the appointed manager and any preliminary employees with the Social Insurance Authority and obtain an employer registration number.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry extract
Incorporation certificate issued by GAFI
Bank certificate showing deposit of the paid capital
Manager's national ID and banking signature card
Lease contract for the registered office
Initial payroll and staffing statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If late registration penalties are imposed, submit a written explanation to the Tax Authority and request an administrative waiver or reduction. If rejected, appeal to the internal tax appeal committee within 30 days of the penalty assessment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial operating license, food safety registration, and civil defense clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA); National Food Safety Authority (NFSA); Civil Defense Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the factory-specific licensing application with IDA, including the architectural layout, machinery list, quick-freezing process description for prepared dim sum and dumplings, food safety plan, and environmental approvals from EEAA. Obtain the Civil Defense fire safety inspection. After the site inspection and NFSA facility registration, IDA will issue the final industrial operating license permitting commercial production.
required_dossiers: IDA industrial license application form
Detailed factory layout and endorsed engineering drawings
Machinery and equipment specification list
Financial statement or bank guarantee where required
Environmental approval issued by the EEAA
Product description and HACCP-based food safety plan
Fire safety and civil defense certificate
Factory lease agreement or land ownership certificate
Occupational health and safety plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the license application is queried, cure technical or documentary deficiencies within the statutory cure period and request a fresh IDA inspection. Any denial of the industrial license may be contested through the IDA Grievance Committee within 30 days of notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA), Ministry of Trade and Industry, jointly with the National Food Safety Authority (NFSA) under Food Safety Law No. 1 of 2017
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Operating License for Foodstuff Manufacturing (Frozen Dim Sum and Dumplings) issued under the Industrial Licensing Law No. 15 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations No. 629 of 2020; NFSA Food Factory Digital Registration

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B (Moderate-Impact Industrial Activity) under Law No. 202 of 2020 and its Executive Regulations; the facility must undergo environmental screening and file an Environmental Assessment Report with limited site-specific impact analysis. Full Category C Environmental Impact Assessment is not required unless the production capacity or discharge loads exceed the regulatory thresholds set by the EEAA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Law No. 202 of 2020 and applicable ministerial decrees. Industrial wastewater discharged into a public sewer must meet: pH 6–9, BOD5 ≤ 60 mg/L, COD ≤ 100 mg/L, TSS ≤ 50 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 5 mg/L. If the plant operates its own treatment and disposal, stricter surface-water discharge limits apply. Stack and fugitive emissions must respect Egyptian ambient air quality limits: PM10 not exceeding 150 µg/m³ daily average, VOC and odor abatement per best available technique; cooling and cooking/steaming exhausts must not cause nuisance. Solid food waste and cooking oil handling must comply with waste segregation and disposal protocols under the waste management regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Civil Defense Administration covering the production building, extinguishing systems, escape routes, storage areas for flammable materials, and employee evacuation plan. Structural load inspection and clearance from the municipal engineering authority or a licensed structural engineer; occupational health and safety clearance from the Ministry of Labour, including machinery guards, noise mitigation, ventilation, and food-handler hygiene. The facility must also complete NFSA food factory registration and pass a physical inspection of floors, walls, drains, and sanitation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance — unified tax administration for corporate income tax, payroll tax, stamp duty and VAT; e-services portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; mandatory e-invoicing/e-receipts platforms: https://einvoicing.invoicing.eta.gov.eg; customs clearance executed through the Egyptian Customs Authority under the Nafeza single-window system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign LLC steps: (1) obtain Commercial Registry extract and investment license from GAFI (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones); (2) submit to ETA the unified tax registration application with constitutional documents, Arabic/Latin certified translations, board resolution appointing a resident tax representative, and notarized power of attorney; (3) obtain the Unified Tax Identification Number (TIN), tax card, and e-invoicing system credentials; (4) simultaneously register for VAT and employer/payroll obligations. TIN issuance is centralized and electronically generated after verification at the competent ETA branch, with Turnaround of 5–15 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — Egyptian LLC is a resident juridical person taxed under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005 at the 22.5% corporate headline rate on worldwide income; non-resident branch taxed on Egypt-source income as a separate deemed entity; no pass-through classification exists for LLCs; SCZone/free-zone licensees may qualify for territorial exemption and a 1% annual charge on export turnover.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists. Available statutory elections: (i) small-business presumptive tax election at 14% on taxable revenue up to EGP 20 million under the 2023 tax facilitation package; (ii) free-zone election under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 substituting income tax with a 1% annual charge on export-related gross revenue; (iii) election for jointly held ventures to be taxed as a separate taxable entity; (iv) participation-exemption election for dividends and capital gains from qualifying shareholdings; (v) advance pricing agreements and bilateral mutual agreement procedure for transfer pricing.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Egyptian Value Added Tax (VAT) — Law No. 67 of 2016 as amended, including the FY2023/24 rate increase to 15%
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory registration where annual taxable supplies of goods or services exceed EGP 500,000 (12-month look-back); voluntary registration available from EGP 50,000; importers and customs declarants must register irrespective of domestic turnover; registration is required before claiming export zero-rating and input VAT refunds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B electronic invoicing through the ETA Electronic Invoicing System, phased in across registered taxpayers; invoices must be submitted in real time via certified ERP/API endpoints in JSON/XML with digital signature, validated against ETA reference data, and stamped with an acceptance code and machine-readable QR; e-receipts for B2C POS transactions are mandated in later phases; non-compliant taxpayers face penalties and suspension of tax clearance certificates.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods qualify for 0% VAT only upon actual physical export outside Egypt evidenced by customs release, shipping documents, and bank remittance; the exporter must hold valid VAT registration, issue export invoices, and retain input tax invoices covering recoverable VAT; offshore services rendered to non-resident customers and performed entirely outside Egypt qualify for zero-rating where the benefit accrues outside Egypt. Frozen dim sum and dumpling products exported as processed food qualify as export of goods under ISIC 1074 manufacturing scope.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export customs invoice and release certificate issued via Egyptian Customs Authority/Nafeza)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing actual exportation and date of shipment
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank receipt evidencing foreign-currency proceeds credited to the exporter's account within 180 days)
Commercial sales invoice, purchase order, and underlying export contract
VAT tax invoices for related input purchases (domestic or import) supporting the input VAT refund calculation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA post-clearance audits verify export authenticity through customs release matching, shipping documents, and FX repatriation within the 180-day deadline; shipments lacking matched inward remittance or customs proof are re-characterized as taxable domestic sales subject to 15% VAT, mandatory clawback of input VAT credits, statutory monthly default interest, and late-payment penalties; fraudulent export documentation triggers criminal prosecution under Articles 38-40 of Law No. 67 of 2016 with imprisonment of up to five years and fines up to three times the evaded tax, plus debarment from e-invoicing, cancellation of the unified tax number, and customs red-flagging of the taxpayer's clearance profile.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), the exclusive foreign exchange administration and monetary authority under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Bank and Banking System Law) and CBE Regulation No. 121 of 2019 on foreign exchange operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt has operated a unified flexible exchange rate regime since March 2024, restoring full interbank determination of the EGP against major foreign currencies. Current account transactions, including trade settlement and distributed profit remittances by non-resident shareholders of an Egyptian LLC, are freely convertible through CBE-authorized dealing banks, subject only to documentary compliance with the Unified Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and CBE reporting forms. Capital account inflows, notably equity injection or capital increases under the Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, remain subject to prior GAFI registration, bank confirmation of the purpose code, and post-transaction CBE statistical reporting. Profit repatriation hurdles are limited to settlement of Egyptian corporate income tax and applicable dividend withholding tax at the rate in force, verification of audited distributable reserves, and evidence that the statutory reserve requirement under Article 87 of Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 has been funded before distribution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE Regulation No. 121 of 2019 as amended by subsequent CBE circulars, all export proceeds must be repatriated to Egypt through an authorized bank and credited to the exporter's foreign currency account within a maximum of 5 months from the bill of lading date. The former mandatory conversion ratios into EGP (ranging from 50 percent to 100 percent of receipts) have been abolished following the March 2024 unification of the exchange rate; the exporter may retain the foreign currency or sell it at the interbank market rate. The CBE retains discretionary authority to reimpose mandatory surrender requirements during future balance-of-payments stress, and all repatriated receipts must be supported by customs declarations, commercial invoices, and the company's official export records at the Egyptian bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (EGP capital deposit before registration) and Operational Current Account with USD sub-account
Operational Current Account and Export Proceeds Foreign Currency Account
Operational Current Account, Trade Finance Facility for Commercial LC and TT, and Hedging Foreign Currency Account
Operational Current Account and SCZONE Corporate Account if licensed in the Suez Canal Economic Zone
Cross-Border Trunking Account with integrated SWIFT MT103 processing and trade services
Operational Current Account and Islamic-compliant current account if required by shareholder mandate

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low. Egypt does not license offshore digital banks or foreign electronic money institutions (EMIs) to hold statutory corporate funds or clear trade payments. Only CBE-licensed payment service providers under the Payment Services Law No. 18 of 2019, acting through a CBE-licensed settlement bank, may provide digital payment accounts, and such accounts are in practice reserved for retail or low-value domestic use. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, and similar platforms) cannot receive statutory export proceeds, cannot remit foreign dividends, and cannot satisfy the CBE export repatriation clock. They are usable only as an ancillary convenience for petty administrative payments outside Egypt; all statutory treasury movements must be routed through the Egyptian banking system.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory in the standard onboarding path. All authorized signatories and each beneficial owner holding not less than 25 percent of the LLC must appear at an Egyptian branch for a biometric identity capture and AML interview. Non-resident directors who cannot travel must execute a notarized power of attorney before an Egyptian consulate or under apostille/legalization procedure, and the shareholders' board resolution must expressly grant account opening authority; at least one natural person signatory must nonetheless appear physically at the branch. Remote and video-only onboarding is recognized only within CBE-approved digital frameworks and is generally unavailable for a foreign-owned corporate capital or trade account, creating a minimum one to two week onboarding timeline and a material notarization cost.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: the bank rejects the LLC because the UBO chain is not fully documented or the ultimate investor is an offshore holding company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate chain chart from each natural person to the LLC; certified memorandum of association; commercial registry extract itemizing all shareholders; passports and residence proofs of all UBOs; audited financial statements of each intermediate holding entity; and a signed written commitment confirming zero bearer shares and zero nominee arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP screening: a non-resident director or UBO appears on a watchlist or the initial capital deposit lacks a verified source of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions clearance reports from UN, EU, UK, OFAC, the CBE terrorism list, and the Egyptian Terrorism Entities List; bank reference letter from the remitting foreign bank; source-of-wealth letter for each UBO; certified gift or loan agreements; and audited financial statements of sister companies or the individual demonstrating lawful origin of the capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade flow mismatch: the bank flags the import of frozen dim sum ingredients and packaging materials as inconsistent with projected export volumes, raising fictitious trade concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documented correspondence between the commercial register scope, GAFI licensing certificate, customs ACI/NAFEZA registration, pro-forma invoices for flour, vegetable oil, seasoning, and cold-chain packaging, valid cold-storage contracts, pre-export inspection certificates issued by the Egyptian Organization for Standardization and Quality (EOS), and a copy of the undrawn LC line confirming genuine trade intent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industry licensing gap: the bank determines that the industrial quick-freezing and frozen food production authorization has not been filed with the regulator.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Industrial production license issued by the Industrial Development Authority (IDA); food safety registration certificate from the National Food Safety Authority (NFSA); label and product composition approval from the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade; factory occupancy certificate; and ISO 22000 or HACCP certification evidencing cold-chain conformity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital account mismatch: the bank refuses to book the equity injection because the GAFI-registered capital increase resolution is filed only after the transfer date.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sequence evidence package comprising the GAFI incorporation certificate, notarized extraordinary general meeting resolution approving the capital increase, bank-generated purpose code declaration identifying the remittance as a capital increase installment, investor's remitting bank reference, and the stamped commercial register deposit certificate matching the exact amount credited, all submitted before the bank release of funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing of the foreign investor's equity injection: first, the LLC obtains a GAFI capital increase certificate, a shareholder resolution, and a purpose code declaration from the receiving CBE-authorized bank classifying the wire as a capital contribution. The remitting foreign bank then executes an SWIFT MT103 to the LLC's account at the Egyptian dealing bank, quoting the LLC full legal name, the commercial registration number, and the Egyptian branch SWIFT/BIC code. The receiving bank verifies that the credited amount matches the GAFI certificate, converts at the interbank market rate if EGP is required, allocates the amount to the capital escrow or capital sub-account, and files the CBE statistical return. Within 90 days the LLC must complete the share capital posting and re-register the commercial record, otherwise the funds are reclassified as shareholder loans and trigger deemed interest and transfer-pricing documentation obligations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements are executed through SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for prepayments and confirmed invoices, and through documentary commercial letters of credit (sight or usance, denominated in USD or EUR) for food-grade ingredient imports. Protocol: register the import in the ACI/NAFEZA platform and obtain the customs code no later than five days pre-shipment; open the LC at the licensed Egyptian bank against the pro-forma invoice, bill of lading, cold-chain certificate, and supplier KYC pack; upon compliant document presentation the bank debits the foreign currency account or sells EGP at the prevailing interbank rate; domestic terminal and cold-chain logistics costs are settled in EGP by direct debit. Exports of frozen dim sum to Middle East and Africa buyers are collected through buyer-issued LCs or incoming telegraphic transfers into the company's foreign currency account, with the CBE five-month repatriation clock running from the bill of lading date; the same rails support toll processing payments to Suez Canal Economic Zone operators.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards on EGP/USD and EGP/EUR, offered by CBE-licensed dealing banks against authenticated underlying trade documentation such as invoices or LCs, typically for tenors up to 12 months.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) referencing the EGP interbank rate, executable offshore through recognized foreign counterparties and generally embedded in a swap structure with the Egyptian bank; standalone onshore NDFs are not permitted.
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCIRS) between USD and EGP for term-matched funding of plant and machinery project finance, subject to a one-time CBE capital approval filing.

Natural hedging through multi-currency operational accounts in USD, EUR, and GBP, enabling matched export receipts and import-related ingredient disbursements without executing an onshore derivative contract.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and supplemental declaration attaching audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Income Tax Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the fiscal year; for a 31 December year-end, filing due by 30 April (one-month extension available upon prior application)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory monthly interest of 2% on unpaid tax plus administrative late-filing penalties of up to EGP 5,000; continued non-compliance permits the ETA to seize bank accounts, suspend tax clearance certificates, and enforce collection procedures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of commercial registration entry (commercial register certificate)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) one-stop shop / Commercial Registry, Ministry of Trade and Industry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due no later than 31 January of each calendar year with reference to the registration anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment fee of approximately EGP 200 per month of delay; non-renewal for two consecutive years results in administrative strike-off of the commercial registration and prohibition from continuing business operations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and update of the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) / Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days of any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership; annual reconfirmation by 30 June of each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or untimely UBO disclosure subjects the LLC to penalties under the Egyptian Anti-Money Laundering Law (Law 80 of 2002), including administrative fines and enhanced regulatory inspection

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent audit by an Egyptian licensed certified auditor is mandatory where annual revenues exceed EGP 10,000,000, paid-up capital exceeds EGP 1,000,000, the number of partners exceeds 10, or the LLC operates under a regulated food-processing license requiring audited financial statements for license renewal
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), substantially aligned with IFRS

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must maintain a physical register of partners and a beneficial-ownership register at its registered office. Any shareholding transfer requires a notarized assignment, board/managerial resolution, and within 15 days an amended commercial registry filing and UBO register update. An annual confirmation statement is filed through GAFI reconfirming all individuals with direct or indirect control of 25% or more of the company.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A 50% tax deduction on taxable profits for up to seven years is available for qualifying labour-intensive and regional investment projects under the Egyptian Investment Law No. 72 of 2017. Additionally, projects licensed to operate in free zones may enjoy a 0% corporate income tax rate on commercial and processing activity; a reduced burden is available in the Suez Canal Economic Zone under specific investment licences.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 20 – Annual Corporate Income Tax Return for Legal Persons, filed electronically via the Egyptian Tax Authority's e-filing platform at www.eta.gov.eg.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within four months following the end of the fiscal year, with a one-month extension available upon a previous written request if audited financial statements are required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the Egyptian Tax Card number, commercial registration number, head office address, and fiscal year-end date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Supply the non-resident parent company's foreign tax identification number, country of tax residence, and complete shareholding details as an attached supplementary sheet.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the aggregate invoiced value of steamed dim sum, dumpling, and food product sales, including export sales and rebates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Export revenues must be supported by bills of lading, customs export documents, and proof of foreign currency remittance to an Egyptian banking account.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare direct material costs, packaging costs, direct labour, factory overheads, and depreciation of production machinery in accordance with Egyptian GAAP and IFRS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All purchases from related parties, including frozen ingredients or packaging materials sourced from the non-resident parent, must be priced at arm's length and supported by intercompany agreements and transfer pricing benchmarks.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List administrative, selling, and distribution expenses, including salaries, rent, utilities, logistics, and executive travel.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management, technical, and royalty fees paid to foreign affiliates must be separately itemized and referenced to withholding tax forms and treaty relief certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 – Taxable Profit Before Loss Offset
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute gross profit minus allowable expenses and non-taxable income to arrive at the pre-offset profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The calculation must ignore any profit or loss attributable to the non-resident owner; only the Egyptian legal entity's own profit and loss position is reportable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply tax losses arising in prior tax years, not exceeding five years, against taxable profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses from the foreign parent or sister companies cannot be used to reduce the Egyptian LLC's taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct any investment-law incentives, free-zone exemptions, or special-area allowances properly verified with the General Authority for Investment (GAFI).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An investment incentive claim must be accompanied by the GAFI licence and annual incentive utilization worksheet; the foreign owner cannot certify the incentive alone.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 22.5% corporate rate to the adjusted taxable income; subtract advance tax instalments and any taxes withheld at source during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withholding credits are limited to Egyptian-sourced withholding; the non-resident parent's home-country dividend or income taxes are not creditable on this return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a fixed administrative fine of EGP 500 plus a monthly surcharge of 2% of the tax due for each month or part-month of delay, capped at 50% of the tax. In addition, late payment of the assessed tax accrues a daily delay interest of 0.3% of the unpaid amount; deliberate non-filing may expose the company to a fine of up to EGP 20,000 and criminal sanctions under Article 133 of Law 91 of 2005.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 20-A – Quarterly Advance Corporate Tax Instalment Schedule, submitted via the Egyptian Tax Authority's e-filing portal and payable at the applicable banking collection points.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Instalments are due no later than the last day of the fourth, seventh, and tenth months of the company's fiscal year; a final balancing payment is filed with the annual Form 20.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Insert the Egyptian Tax Card number and fiscal year for which the advance calculation is made.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The schedule must be signed by the Egyptian legal representative or tax agent; non-resident directors are not expected to sign unless resident in Egypt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provide a good-faith projection of current-year pre-tax profit based on rolling six-month actuals.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The forecast cannot be suppressed via related-party expenses or royalties; excessive underpayment invites transfer pricing audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the final taxable profit and tax payable from the preceding audited year as the default basis for instalment calculation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident owner's takeover or restructuring in the current year does not reset the instalment base; the prior-year tax remains the benchmark until an amendment is accepted by the Egyptian Tax Authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicate one-quarter of the estimated annual tax due for the current year, or the statutorily prescribed percentage of the prior-year liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: At least one instalment must be funded from the company's Egyptian bank account; direct payment by the foreign parent will be reclassified as a shareholder contribution or income depending on evidence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment or underpayment of a quarterly instalment carries a monthly delay surcharge of 2% of the tax due, plus a delay penalty of 0.5% per day on the unpaid balance; repeated defaults authorize the Egyptian Tax Authority to issue an administrative seizure order against the factory's bank accounts and movable assets.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (final withholding) on dividends paid by an Egyptian LLC to non-resident shareholders; no Egyptian withholding is applied to dividends distributed to resident Egyptian corporate shareholders or to qualifying free-zone entities when exemption applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced rate under a double taxation agreement, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit to the Egyptian Tax Authority: (a) a written relief application using the standard non-resident withholding tax form; (b) a valid certificate of tax residence issued by the competent tax authority of the treaty country for the relevant calendar year, legalised and apostilled where required; (c) a declaration of beneficial ownership and supporting evidence of real economic activity; and (d) the underlying distribution resolution and contract documentation. The Egyptian LLC payer must retain the approved relief certificate and attach a copy to its withholding tax return; if relief at source is not obtained before distribution, the non-resident must file a refund application within five years from the end of the fiscal year in which the tax was withheld.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for trademarks, patents, technology, software licences, and know-how paid to non-residents are subject to a 20% statutory withholding tax, with treaty rates typically between 5% and 15% if a beneficial-ownership test is satisfied. Interest on foreign shareholder loans and other non-resident debt financing is subject to a statutory withholding tax of 15%, though a 20% rate applies to certain non-financial counterparties; most Egyptian treaties reduce interest withholding to rates ranging from 0% to 15%.

approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Egyptian Tax Authority does not apply a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) framework equivalent to those in the UAE or Bahrain; however, it enforces substance-over-form, generally accepted GAAR principles, beneficial-ownership requirements under double tax treaties, and requires companies to maintain actual managerial, operational, and payroll substance in Egypt to withstand treaty benefit and transfer pricing challenges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – False or Concealed Records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally understating revenue from dim sum/dumpling sales, fabricating supplier invoices, running unrecorded cash or e-wallet collections, or destroying production records and inventory logs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment for a term not exceeding five years and a fine equal to the amount of evaded tax plus additional civil penalties of 100% to 200% of the assessed tax; the Egyptian Tax Authority may also freeze bank accounts, confiscate transportation assets, and suspend the factory's commercial registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false returns, participate in off-book sales, or allow fraudulent export declarations to be lodged may be jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and fines, subject to travel bans (preventive seizure of passport), and may face criminal imprisonment alongside the company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering an Egyptian LLC with no independent local management, no factory floor staff, no physical production premises, and routing purchase/selling transactions through the shell solely to obtain Egyptian treaty benefits on foreign income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the shell arrangement for corporate income tax purposes, re-attribution of profits to the actual foreign parent, denial of treaty relief, and a penalty of 20% of the adjusted revenue plus interest; free-zone privileges can be revoked by GAFI where the entity lacks genuine local functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil will be pierced if the shareholder-director used the LLC as an instrument of tax fraud; personal liability extends to restitution of evaded taxes, disqualification from board service in Egypt, and criminal proceedings involving administrative sanctions up to imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the related-party transaction schedule, charging artificial PPR/raw-material prices above arm's length, paying excessive royalty or management fee to the non-resident parent, or omitting the mandatory local and master file when transactions exceed EGP 5,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Egyptian Tax Authority may perform a unilateral adjustment to taxable profit plus priming interest, impose a misdeclaration penalty between 20% and 200% of the undercharged tax, and levy administrative fines up to EGP 200,000 for documentation failure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved fabricated related-party contracts or instructed the accountant to conceal the parent-supplier relationship may be personally liable for the assessed adjustment and penalties, and may be subject to criminal sanction if the misdeclaration is tied to fraudulent letters of credit or money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends or making royalty/interest payments to non-resident shareholders and foreign lenders without applying the required 10%, 20%, or 15% withholding and without obtaining treaty relief certification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Egyptian LLC is liable as payer for the uncollected withholding tax plus a delay surcharge of 2% per month and a fixed penalty of EGP 5,000; the non-resident recipient may be deemed ineligible for treaty benefits and become taxable in Egypt on a deemed assessed basis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The senior finance director and the chairman are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid withholding tax because the law expressly imposes personal liability on the custodian of corporate funds who has not caused the tax to be withheld and remitted; criminal prosecution may include travel restrictions and confiscation of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring export proceeds from frozen dim sum products through personal accounts, using unofficial currency-exchange markets, or accepting unaccounted cash from domestic distributors to avoid tax, notwithstanding the entity's Low_Risk_Standard banking tier.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Breach of Egyptian Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002 exposes the company and its responsible officers to fines ranging from EGP 100,000 to EGP 1,000,000 and imprisonment of one to seven years; the Supreme Council for Economic Courts may order liquidation and asset forfeiture.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally engaged in the movement of proceeds through private overseas accounts are subject to arrest, free travel-bank confirmation, confiscation of passport, freeze of UAE and international bank relationships, and personal criminal convictions; the corporate veil is lifted to deem the company's assets as the director's fraudulent vault.
